news.title: Israel's Under-20 footballers and a golden generation of hope and talent
news.lede: A team that offered hope... then, four months later, Hamas attacked Israel. It was, says Ido Rakovsky, like reporting on "science fiction", rather than sport. Israel, whose senior team have qualified for the World Cup just once, had beaten global powerhouses Brazil in the quarter-finals of the under-20 version of the tournament. At the final whistle, the commentator covering the match for Israeli television vowed "you will tell of this night to your children, and they will tell it to your grandchildren".

news.title: World Cup Final should be at Barcelona’s Camp Nou, says Joan Laporta
news.lede: “It shouldn’t be Casablanca or Madrid; it should be the Spotify Camp Nou.” That’s how FC Barcelona’s president, Joan Laporta, put it, in an interview with Spanish radio. He wants the FIFA World Cup final to be played at Barcelona’s refurbished home, urging football’s governing body to pass over Madrid, Spain’s capital, and Casablanca, Morocco’s largest city. He jokingly dismissed those rival bids, saying “Casablanca and Madrid are the same thing.”

news.title: ‘My scar, not your scar’: Tuchel stands by England semi-final subs but admits wrong timing
news.lede: Coach says Argentina’s gung-ho approach forced hand. ‘No one is more hurt than me, no one wanted it more’. Thomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina this summer, but the England head coach accepts he made them too early. Tuchel said England were “waiting for death”, unable to cope with the attacking tactics adopted by Argentina in Atlanta as they chased the game after Anthony Gordon’s opener on the hour.

news.title: New Zealand U-17 men’s team visit Japan for World Cup preparation
news.lede: New Zealand’s U-17 men will begin an important phase of their FIFA World Cup preparations when they open a three-match tournament in Japan. Head coach Martin Bullock’s 18-player squad will face hosts Niigata, Myanmar and Japan at the International Youth Soccer Tournament in Niigata. The tournament provides New Zealand with competitive international football two months before the FIFA U-17 Men’s World Cup in Qatar. The squad prepared for Japan with two matches between academy teams from Wellington Phoenix and Auckland United at the NZCIS facility in Trentham last weekend.

news.title: World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente extends Spain contract to 2032
news.lede: Luis de la Fuente's new contract will extend his tenure as Spain head coach to 10 years. World Cup-winning head coach Luis de la Fuente has agreed a contract extension with Spain until 2032. The 65-year-old's previous deal was due to expire in 2028. De la Fuente, who guided Spain to their fourth European Championship title in 2024 before securing global honours this summer, is now set to remain in charge for Spain's World Cup defence on home soil in 2030.

news.title: Spain rewards Luis de la Fuente with new contract after World Cup 2026 victory
news.lede: September 16, 2026 Austine Agbo Emmanuel Sports 0. Spain have confirmed that head coach Luis de la Fuente has renewed his contract with the national team, keeping him in charge until 2030 as the Spanish Football Federation continues to build around the coach who has overseen a highly successful period for La Roja. The contract extension means De la Fuente is set to remain at the helm through the next major international cycle, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup and the 2028 European Championship, with his new deal running until 2030. De la Fuente took charge of Spain’s senior national team in December 2022 after previously working extensively within the country’s youth setup.

news.title: FIFA moves to review Infantino’s shelved World Cup investment plan amid scrutiny
news.lede: September 16, 2026 Adejayan Gbenga Sports 0. FIFA has confirmed that a review of the withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise investment proposal will be presented to the FIFA Council amid growing criticism over the controversial plan. The development followed criticism from Danish Football Association president Jesper Moller, who accused FIFA of failing to provide answers to what he described as “critical questions” surrounding the shelved proposal. FIFA said the matter would be reviewed in accordance with its governance procedures, with the findings eventually presented to the FIFA Council.

news.title: USA exit U-20 World Cup on penalties as tournament’s timing draws criticism
news.lede: Brazil advance to quarter-finals in Poland. Americans have not won tournament since 2012. US youth teams have struggled in recent showings. The United States were eliminated from the U-20 Women’s World Cup in the last 16 on Wednesday, falling to Brazil on penalties after playing to a 1-1 draw after extra-time.
